title: GENT Vigilon
subtitle: Full-size 4/6-loop family - July 2015 operator profile

modelScope.variant: Full-size EN Vigilon 4/6-loop panel with 2 km loop cards
modelScope.menuMapFirmware: EN54 (V4), MCC/MCB V4.53 or higher as printed in Appendix A-1
modelScope.editionBoundary: This is the July 2015 classic full-size family, not a claimed match for Vigilon Plus, Compact, Compact VA, Nano or every later firmware revision.
modelScope.practiceConfiguration: Fictional single local panel, two commissioned loops, three zones, six devices; integral printer fitted and initially off.
modelScope.selectionReason: The operator manual and matching dated generic menu appendix provide strong, inspectable source coverage; no market-share claim is made.

sources.title: Vigilon panel and Network node - Operating instructions
sources.edition: July 2015; printed footer issue 4_07-15; metadata and preface describe issue 2
sources.hostType: Manufacturer document mirrored by a fire-system installer
sources.note: Primary operator procedure source. Several internal inconsistencies are explicitly recorded in the audit.

sources.title: Generic Commissioning Instructions for Vigilon 4/6 loop & Compact range of fire panels & network nodes
sources.originalUrlStatus: Returned 404 when independently opened during this audit
sources.hostType: Original Gent manual downloaded from an archive mirror
sources.note: Appendix A-1 covers EN54 (V4) Vigilon with MCC/MCB V4.53 or higher. Compact VA-only and fitted-option branches are excluded or marked conditional. The working archive URL is used for page links.

sources.title: Vigilon VIG1-24 and VIG1-72 installation instructions
sources.note: Printed p12 and pp15-16 confirm up to four/six loop circuits, up to 200 devices per loop and 32-character device / 28-character MCP labels; p48 identifies the issue.

sources.title: Vigilon Plus — Basic Commissioning Training
sources.edition: Undated manufacturer training presentation; archive filename labels it 2017
sources.hostType: Manufacturer-origin training presentation mirrored by FACP Manuals
sources.note: Page 103 corroborates Test/Eng > Test > Test > On/Off > direct zone-number entry > Enter. The visible slide has no separate Zone button or Loop step. Used only to interpret the matching 2015 menu-map structure; this does not change the classic VIG1-24/VIG1-72 profile to Vigilon Plus. The archive says 2017, but reviewed slides have no confirmed manufacturer issue date; PDF CreationDate is 2021-06-07 and ModDate is 2026-02-02. Do not claim a verified 2017 edition or physical-panel validation.

leds.label: Fault
leds.meaning: A fault is present in the system.

leds.label: Power Fault
leds.meaning: A mains or battery supply fault is present.

leds.label: System Fault
leds.meaning: The system processor has a fault; detection performance may be affected.

leds.label: Delay
leds.meaning: One or more delay blocks are configured. The operator p9 table mistakenly repeats the Sounder label for this row; the p7 face labels it Delay.

leds.label: Test
leds.meaning: One or more zones are in Test mode.

leds.label: Disablement
leds.meaning: Part of the system is disabled.

leds.label: Fire
leds.meaning: A fire condition has been detected.

leds.label: Verify
leds.meaning: The commissioned Verify facility is extending the sounder delay.

leds.label: Sounder
leds.meaning: Flashes for sounder fault; steady for sounder disablement, with the corresponding common indicator.

leds.label: Fire Routing O/P Active
leds.meaning: The output to Fire Alarm Routing Equipment is active.

leds.label: Fire Routing O/P Fault/Dis
leds.meaning: Flashing with Disablement means disabled; steady with Fault means a FARE fault.

leds.label: Power
leds.meaning: A supply to the panel is present.

nodes.title: Main menu
nodes.note: The four physical function buttons select the prompts above them. Menu On/Off aborts a menu operation; it is not a Back button.

nodes.title: Control
nodes.note: This training profile uses a customer access code. Protected Enable and Disable choices are entered after UserCode. The practice printer is fitted but initially switched off.

nodes.title: Enter access code
nodes.note: FINDR practice code 2468. It is fictional and is not a Gent default or a live-site access code.

nodes.title: Additional Control functions
nodes.note: The commissioning map includes Sector, MSector, FARE, Sounder, Aux Rly, Timeslot, DelayBlk, Pause, Build, Sound, Silence, Reset, Verify, Digital, Voice, StartMA and StopMA. Access and fitted options change what appears. The FARE selection key conflicts between the operating text and map, so these routes are shown in the source map without a fabricated key drill.

nodes.title: Enable
nodes.note: Zone is the second function button after one <etc>. Sector and Group are source-reference branches in this trainer.

nodes.title: Enable

nodes.title: Enable

nodes.title: Enable
nodes.note: Audio belongs to the Compact VA variant and is excluded from this full-size panel profile.

nodes.title: Enable sensing - device
nodes.fieldHelp: Enter a single device address from the fictional site directory. The operator examples use 1-200; the generic map uses 1-207. No range entry is simulated.

nodes.title: Enable sensing - loop
nodes.note: Sensing disablement is not the same as disabling a device sounder. A manual call point is only individually addressable for disablement; the lessons use a detector.
nodes.fieldHelp: This commissioned training site has loops 1 and 2. This is a site fixture, not the capacity limit of a 4/6-loop panel.

nodes.title: Enable zone
nodes.note: The zone lesson uses Zone 2, which contains no manual call point. The exact manual-call-point treatment under zone disablement is not asserted for this edition.
nodes.fieldHelp: Enter one commissioned zone. The manual permits zones 1-128; the fictional site has zones 1-3.

nodes.title: Enable IO Line
nodes.note: Requires I/O line, device and loop. An output line assigned to a sector can only be disabled through that sector, which also affects its other devices. Site cause-and-effect is not modelled.

nodes.title: Enable Sounders
nodes.note: Separate from sensing disablement. The menu map specifies sounder and loop parameters; sounder assignment and all-device effects require site-specific evidence.

nodes.title: Enable Sector
nodes.note: Engineering level branch in the generic menu map. A sector can contain multiple devices and outputs; it is not interchangeable with a detection zone.

nodes.title: Enable Group
nodes.note: Source-listed group enable/disable option. Membership is specific to the installed configuration.

nodes.title: Enable Build
nodes.note: Source-listed command-build enable/disable option. The command definition is site-specific.

nodes.title: Enable FARE
nodes.note: Fire Alarm Routing Equipment enable/disable is distinct from manually switching its output On/Off. The operator manual explicitly says not to use Sector disablement to disable FARE.

nodes.title: Enable FPE
nodes.note: Applies to Fire Protection Equipment interfaces. Effects depend on the connected fire protection equipment and commissioned logic.

nodes.title: Enable Aux Rly
nodes.note: Two auxiliary relays provide voltage-free contacts. Operator p28 says F2 after three <etc> presses, while the appendix places AuxRly third after FARE and FPE; the simulator does not guess this disputed route.

nodes.title: Enable Comms
nodes.note: Source-listed communication enable/disable option. The map uses card and port selectors; these are not simulated as a working network.

nodes.title: Status
nodes.note: The source map documents Device, Sector, Card, Zone, Group, Network, SectLink, DelayLink, Sounders, TimeSlot, DelayBlk, AuxRly, Build, DST, FARE and FPE status. Engineering measurements and live network status are reference only.

nodes.title: Enter access code
nodes.note: Fictional FINDR practice code: 2468.

nodes.title: Set Up
nodes.note: Save is the customer-level persistence operation. The separate Enter branch belongs to configuration work; use Modify to change a label.

nodes.title: Set Up - Enter
nodes.note: The generic map lists Enter beside Modify, but the operator label-edit procedures use Modify. No alternate configuration-entry workflow is invented.

nodes.title: Set Up - engineering branches
nodes.note: Assign, Remove, Set Up, Action, Deaction, Backup, Recover and Protect are engineer configuration branches. The complete source map is available in the menu reference; the customer code does not grant engineering access.

nodes.title: Set Clock
nodes.note: Field order: hour, minute, date, month, year. Enter commits the practice clock. The manual then instructs the user to Save. Clock and daylight-saving setup are configuration-dependent on a real system.

nodes.title: Save to memory
nodes.note: Changes to labels, password and clock settings require Save. The operator manual permits this only when there are no disablements present. Saving here affects only the fictional practice site.

nodes.title: Modify
nodes.note: Sound and signal-period configuration branches shown in the generic map require engineering access and are not offered to the customer profile.

nodes.title: Modify MCP label
nodes.note: The appendix has an MCP branch. The operating manual explicitly allows a manual call point label through Device, with a 28-character maximum; that verified Device route is the implemented route.

nodes.title: Modify label - device
nodes.fieldHelp: Enter one device address from the site directory.

nodes.title: Modify label - loop
nodes.fieldHelp: This fictional commissioned site uses loop 1 or 2.

nodes.title: Modify device label
nodes.note: Physical Enter confirms the label; F2 is not the label commit key. Maximum 32 characters for a device, 28 for an MCP. Save is required afterward.

nodes.title: Modify label - zone
nodes.fieldHelp: Enter the detection zone number.

nodes.title: Modify zone label
nodes.note: Physical Enter confirms the 32-character maximum label; then Save.

nodes.title: Modify local panel label

nodes.title: Modify custom label
nodes.note: The custom label is displayed beneath the standards line on the panel. Confirm with physical Enter, then Save.

nodes.title: Modify label - IO line
nodes.note: The operator edit procedure specifies F3 Device here; the view-I/O procedure uses F2. These routes intentionally retain that difference.

nodes.title: Enter access code
nodes.note: Fictional FINDR customer practice code 2468 opens the existing customer menu. The separate fictional engineering practice code 3917 opens the walk-test branch only. Neither is a Gent default or a live-site credential.

nodes.title: Test/Eng - customer access
nodes.note: The operator password-change procedure explicitly specifies F1 NewPass after UserCode. The repair page instead says F1 Loop and has another incorrect top-level key; its path is held for verification rather than guessed.

nodes.title: NewPass
nodes.note: The documented route changes the site customer PIN using physical Enter and requires a memory Save. FINDR uses one explicitly fictional training credential and does not teach or change a real panel credential.

nodes.title: Zone Test
nodes.note: The original narrative abbreviates the route differently from the diagram. The working walk-test branch now follows the complete 2015 p105 map: Test/Eng > Test > Test > On/Off > zone-number entry > Enter, corroborated by the separate manufacturer training slide. This retained reference explains the earlier source limitation; it is not an alternative key route.

nodes.title: Loop Repair
nodes.note: A wiring fault must be physically corrected by the servicing engineer before Repair. The operator page has conflicting key instructions and loop limits; this is a source-reference topic, not an operational key drill.

nodes.title: Printer
nodes.note: When on, F3 is Off; when off, F3 is On. Test prints a character sample and Paper Fd performs eight line feeds in the documented panel. The simulator records a fictional printout only.

scenarios.title: Panel healthy
scenarios.description: Start with no fire, faults, disablements or tests.

scenarios.title: One fire input
scenarios.description: Reception sensor is active. Silence and Reset can be practised, and an active input can cause the fire indication to return.

scenarios.title: Three fire events
scenarios.description: The first fire stays pinned while Previous and Next scroll the two later fire events.

scenarios.title: A device fault
scenarios.description: A fictional office sensor removal fault. Cancel Buzzer acknowledges the sound; Reset does not repair the device.

scenarios.title: Sensing disabled
scenarios.description: Loop 1 Device 1 sensing is disabled. Practise restoring it.

scenarios.title: Zone disabled
scenarios.description: Zone 2 is disabled. It contains no MCP, so the disputed MCP-in-zone behaviour is outside this lesson.

scenarios.title: Fire, fault and disablement
scenarios.description: A fire and a separate fault remain visible while Zone 2 is disabled. Practise interpreting concurrent indicators and active events.

scenarios.title: Walk test active — Zone 2
scenarios.description: Zone 2 starts in test with normal inputs. Practise the separate engineering Off route, then verify the Test indicator is out.

trainingPolicies.walkTestConfirmation: FINDR supplies concise Zone Test On/Off confirmation wording; an exact firmware confirmation display is not claimed.

menuReferenceNote: Reference routes catalogue named menu branches. Numeric parameter-entry stages and repeated paging steps are not all expanded. Exact function-key sequences are asserted only by the verified interactive nodes; conditional and engineering routes retain their source-map limits.

knownLimits.summary: PDF metadata title and preface say issue 2 / second issue, while the final printed footer says issue 4_07-15.
knownLimits.treatment: Identify the source by document number, July 2015, panel scope and SHA256; preserve both issue descriptions.

knownLimits.summary: Full-size operator instructions repeatedly use loop 1-2 despite p22 describing cards 1-4 and up to six for VIG1-72. Generic appendix selectors allow 1-8.
knownLimits.treatment: The fictional commissioned site has only loops 1 and 2. No claim that two or eight is the hardware capacity of the selected 4/6-loop panel.

knownLimits.summary: Operator device range is 1-200; generic appendix parameter boxes use 1-207.
knownLimits.treatment: Operator forms use the documented 1-200 range and validate against the fictional installed devices. Extended/reserved addresses are not assumed.

knownLimits.summary: Repair p38 says F1 Test/Eng, contradicting the visible F4 top-level mapping, and says F1 Loop after UserCode where PIN-change p21 specifies F1 NewPass.
knownLimits.treatment: Repair is reference-only, with no fabricated exact button lesson.

knownLimits.summary: The narrative on p81 abbreviates and orders the selectors differently from the complete p105 diagram. A manufacturer training slide independently shows both Test selections followed by On/Off, direct zone-number entry and Enter.
knownLimits.treatment: Use the complete 2015 p105 branch and document the p103 training-slide corroboration. There is no additional Zone function-key selection or Loop step. The profile remains classic EN54 (V4), MCC/MCB V4.53+, and has not been validated against a physical panel.

knownLimits.summary: Operator p26 says choose FARE with F4 after cycling <etc>; the generic control map positions FARE before <etc>.
knownLimits.treatment: FARE output On/Off is a source-reference branch.

knownLimits.summary: Operator p28 says Aux Rly is F2 after three <etc> presses. p27 says FPE is F2; the appendix page places FARE,FPE,AuxRly in that order.
knownLimits.treatment: Show appendix order in the reference map; Aux Rly operation remains reference-only.

knownLimits.summary: July 2015 operator text describes individual MCP sensing disablement but does not explicitly state MCP behaviour when a zone is disabled. An older 1999 manual differs in scope and is not silently imported.
knownLimits.treatment: The zone-disable lesson uses Zone 2, with no MCP. Full MCP-in-zone behaviour requires panel-specific confirmation.

knownLimits.summary: The p9 indicator table calls the delay-block row Sounder; the physical-face illustration labels it Delay.
knownLimits.treatment: Use the physical-face Delay label and explain its delay-block meaning.

knownLimits.summary: The face artwork repeats 30 in the 17-32 zone row.
knownLimits.treatment: Render the normal continuous zone numbers 1-32 and disclose the artwork discrepancy here.

knownLimits.summary: Within the FPE procedure one line says FARE while its headings, choice and confirmation all say FPE.
knownLimits.treatment: Keep FPE terminology based on the explicit heading, selector and confirmation; FPE operation is reference-only.

knownLimits.summary: View IO label uses F2 Device; Edit IO label explicitly uses F3 Device.
knownLimits.treatment: Preserve each printed route rather than standardising the two.

knownLimits.summary: Display/Print selection is skipped if the printer is absent or switched off.
knownLimits.treatment: Start with a fitted printer switched off and dynamically include output selection when switched on.

knownLimits.summary: AL1, AL2a, AL2b and AL3 have different visibility. Compact VA, D1 voice, SD card, radio, network and Freeblock conditions introduce further branches.
knownLimits.treatment: Customer routes remain interactive. Only the sourced zone walk-test engineering branch is added behind a distinct fictional practice credential. Other engineering and fitted-option operations remain references.

knownLimits.summary: The keyboard includes Insert, Delete, Shift and cursor keys; the operator text does not fully specify cursor editing semantics.
knownLimits.treatment: FINDR uses a documented training text editor and enforces source label limits; no claim of byte-for-byte firmware editing behaviour.

knownLimits.summary: Display test and Zone Test have approximate documented durations; real alarm behaviour depends on commissioning.
knownLimits.treatment: Use training timing and distinguish rising hint tones from physical panel sounds.

knownLimits.summary: The source documents the clock-field order and controls but does not specify a permitted year range.
knownLimits.treatment: The practice date editor uses 2000-2099 as an explicit FINDR calendar limit, not a claimed Gent hardware or firmware limit.

knownLimits.summary: Params, Cancel and Quit exist in the documentation, but their exact function-key positions are not established independently for every form.
knownLimits.treatment: Live forms show individually verified function-key positions. The p105 zone-entry row explicitly supplies F2 Enter, F3 Cancel and F4 Quit. FINDR clearing an uncommitted draft on Cancel is a declared editing convention; it never ends a committed test selection. Additional Params behaviour remains reference-only.

knownLimits.summary: The source allows zone ranges and describes additional installation-dependent output inhibition. FINDR exercises one installed zone at a time; external plant, delay blocks, network functions and real protective outputs are not simulated. An active test input must be restored before Off; that transition restriction and concise confirmation wording are FINDR policies.
knownLimits.treatment: Teach the physical start/end key path, five-second test cycle, persistent Test indication and explicit restoration without claiming full firmware or external-output fidelity. The Cancel key clears only an uncommitted FINDR draft.
